Within that organization, the Network Security team designs and defends the network infrastructure connecting Millennium's global offices, data centers, and cloud environments, spanning perimeter controls such as firewalls, IDS/IPS, NDR, NAC, proxies, email security, and DNS security, as well as the detection and automation stack behind them, including the security data lake, logging pipelines, and SOAR automations. This is a growing organization that combines deep technical expertise with pragmatic risk management to keep pace with the speed and scale of the firm's business. What You'll Do Design, implement, and maintain network security controls, including firewalls, segmentation, secure remote access, intrusion detection and prevention, network detection and response, and network access control, and support secure network architecture for new offices, data centers, and cloud connectivity. Build and maintain the logging pipelines and security data lake that power detection across the environment. Develop, implement, and maintain security policies, procedures, and standards across network security, email security, DNS security, and the security data lake. Strengthen perimeter security through automation, improved monitoring, vulnerability identification, and actionable alerting and reporting. Monitor, manage, and analyze security logs, alerts, and events across multiple systems to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and suspicious activity, and tune network infrastructure to reduce risk while minimizing business disruption. Apply AI to the team's own work, accelerating investigation, automation, detection engineering, and reporting, and help secure the firm's use of AI models, tools, and frameworks. Conduct system audits and vulnerability assessments, manage remediation efforts and findings from audits, penetration tests, and process reviews, participate in incident response for network-related events, and use threat intelligence to sharpen detection, defense, and response. Hands-on experience administering enterprise network security infrastructure, including firewalls, VPN, proxies, intrusion detection and prevention, network detection and response, and network access control, with a practical understanding of proxy engineering concepts. Proven experience as a security engineer with hands-on expertise in logging pipelines, data lakes, or SIEM platforms such as Splunk, ELK, Sentinel, or S3/Athena, plus SOAR automation; experience with breach and attack simulation tooling is a plus. Hands-on AI experience, both using AI tooling in day-to-day security work and securing the use, deployment, and governance of AI models, tools, and frameworks. Strong command of core networking and infrastructure concepts, including TCP/IP, routing, switching, segmentation, DNS, Wi-Fi, and virtualization, along with email and DNS security controls and packet capture and network analysis tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, or ngrep. Experience securing hybrid on-premises and cloud network architectures, with working knowledge of AWS, GCP, or Azure and proficiency across Windows, Linux, macOS, and container environments such as Docker and Kubernetes. Scripting or development skills in Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar languages, with the ability to troubleshoot complex network and security issues under time pressure, operate independently in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment, and communicate clearly with both deeply technical teams and senior executive stakeholders. Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity/Information Security, or a related field, or commensurate work experience; certifications such as CISSP, GCIA, CISM, CCNP Security, Palo Alto PCNSE, or Fortinet NSE are valued.
